| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Services      | Each Traffic Monitor service: running, stopped, starting, or running after restarts that followed failures. Frigate restarts itself when you save its config; that doesn't count as a failure. When it restarts itself again and again within minutes, as when its AI accelerator has failed, that does count, and the row says so.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Apps          | Frigate answers, isn't in safe mode (with no cameras because of a config error), and gets frames from each camera. When Frigate stopped on an error, the Frigate check quotes it. When Frigate isn't answering because it keeps stopping itself, the check says so and points at the Hardware group and the diagnostics. Node-RED answers, loaded `config.yml` without errors, and has its database at the version this install expects. The camera streams run, and Frigate reads them. The MQTT broker requires its login while port 1883 is open to the network.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Configuration | Frigate and `config.yml` agree on the names that link them: each Frigate camera is enabled in `config.yml`, it has the zones `zone_capture`, `zone_near`, `zone_far`, and `zone_radar`, each radar under `sensors.radars` is named after one of the `TM_RADAR_SERIAL_PORT_` variables in `node-red-tm.env`, and each camera's radar is enabled. The Location check is a problem when a `deployment` value in `config.yml` is one Node-RED won't accept, such as a coordinate out of range or a bearing with spaces around it, and names the key. It warns when a sensor still has its own `lat` or `lon`, when the device's places haven't been set up since an update, which the control app does by itself once Node-RED answers, and when `survey_id` names a place the device doesn't have, and links to the [Location page](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/location/index.md). In safe mode Frigate has no cameras, so the checks that read them, here and in the Apps group, report that they couldn't run and point at the Frigate check. It also checks the ThingsBoard upload: its settings, and that a token is set when the upload is on. The Frigate+ check says whether a Frigate+ key and a Frigate+ model are set together, and whether Frigate can use the model; see [The Frigate+ check](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/configuration/frigate-config/#the-frigate-check). See [config.yml settings](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/configuration/node-red-config/index.md) and [First-time setup](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/setup-guide/index.md). |
| Hardware      | Each AI accelerator, from plugged in to passed to Frigate and listed in its config, or a warning when there's none and Frigate detects on the CPU. Whether detection works is Frigate's to report: when its detector keeps failing, Frigate restarts itself, and the Services and Apps rows say so. The video decoder Frigate uses for the camera. Each radar, from plugged in to read by Node-RED.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Network       | The device's [Wi-Fi](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/wifi-hotspot/index.md), in four checks. An offline device is normal, so none of them is a problem for lack of internet. See [The Network group](#the-network-group).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Device        | Free storage (a warning under 2 GB, a problem under 512 MB), free memory (a warning under 200 MB), the processor's temperature (a warning from 80 °C, a problem from 85 °C), and the power supply: whether the Pi ran short of power or slowed itself down since it started.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Date and time | Whether the clock was ever set, and whether it keeps time from the internet.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

### The Network group

| Check         | What it says                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hotspot       | **On as `TM-4F2A`, at `http://10.42.0.1/`** while the hotspot is up. **Standing by** while the device is on a saved network; the hotspot starts when that network is out of reach. **Off by choice** when the hotspot is turned off. A problem when the hotspot isn't set up (rerun the installer with `-t wifi`), the Wi-Fi radio is switched off, the hotspot should be on and isn't (**Restart the hotspot**), the hotspot has no password (**Set a password** opens the [Network page](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/wifi-hotspot/#change-the-password); see also [A hotspot you set up by hand](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/wifi-hotspot/#a-hotspot-you-set-up-by-hand)), a USB Wi-Fi adapter has taken the built-in radio's place, or the hotspot's firewall isn't loaded. A warning when the hotspot isn't secured with WPA2. |
| Wi-Fi network | The network the device is on and its signal, or that it has no saved network, or that none of the saved networks is in reach. The [Network page](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/wifi-hotspot/#saved-networks) lists the saved networks and lets an administrator join a network, reorder them, and forget them.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Internet      | **Reachable**, or **Not reachable. That's normal for an offline unit.** It also says when the network needs a sign-in page, so the device has no internet. It is never a warning or a problem.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Wi-Fi country | The country, or a warning that none is set. Rerun the installer with `-t wifi` and it asks; see [The Wi-Fi country](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/wifi-hotspot/#the-wi-fi-country).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

A check that can't read the Wi-Fi state shows a question mark.

### Fix a problem

A check that isn't passing offers one of these:

- **A Restart button**, such as **Restart Frigate**, for a service that stopped or keeps failing. The Hotspot check's **Restart the hotspot** has the device look at its Wi-Fi radio and start the hotspot if it should be on. The device asks first and says what you'll notice, for example that traffic isn't counted while Frigate restarts. A note under the button says when the restart is under way.
- **Re-scan hardware**, at the end of the Hardware group while one of its checks isn't passing. It runs every check again at once, so you don't wait for the next check after you plug a device back in or follow the check's advice.
- **A link** to the page that fixes it, such as **Set the date and time**, **Diagnostics** on the Device page, or **Set the token** for the ThingsBoard upload, which opens [Tokens and keys](#tokens-and-keys), or **Set the key** for Frigate+, which opens the Frigate+ API key section of the [Detection page](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/detection/#frigate-plus), or **Open the Location page** for the Location check.
- **A sentence** with the next step, such as rerunning the installer for Node-RED (`tmsetup.sh -t node-red-tm`; see [Installer options](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/reference/tmsetup/index.md)).

The control app can't restart itself. If it stops, see [If the control app is down](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/control-app/#if-the-control-app-is-down).

## The Device page

The card at the top shows the device's name, its Raspberry Pi model and memory, the Traffic Monitor version, the serial number, how long it has been running, its free storage, the processor's temperature, and the power supply's state. It also lists each connected link, Ethernet or Wi-Fi, with its IP address and MAC address, and **Network details** opens the [Network page](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/wifi-hotspot/#the-network-page). If the device can't read its network state, the card leaves the list out. **Software** lists the versions of Frigate, Node-RED, go2rtc, nginx, and the Hailo driver if installed, the Traffic Monitor commit, the operating system, and the kernel.

### Tokens and keys

Administrators set the credentials the device uses for outside services in **Tokens and keys**. The section is closed when the page opens; select its heading to open it. The Status page's **Set the token** link opens it for you. It lists the ThingsBoard access token, and the Plate Recognizer API token and license key when the [Plate Recognizer](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/add-ons/plate-recognizer/index.md) add-on is installed. Each is kept with the device's other secrets, not in `config.yml`. The [Frigate+](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/configuration/frigate-config/#better-models) API key is on the [Detection page](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/detection/#frigate-plus), next to the models it fetches.

- A value is never shown back. The page says whether it's set and, for a token or key of 12 or more characters, its last four characters, so you can tell which one you entered. It never shows any of the license key.
- **Save** stores what you typed in the box. The eye icon shows it while you type. A ThingsBoard token takes letters, digits, and `. _ ~ -`. A Plate Recognizer value takes printable ASCII characters without spaces. Both are up to 256 characters long.
- **Remove** asks first, then empties the value. Without a ThingsBoard token the upload stops, and without the Plate Recognizer values plates aren't read.
- Saving or removing restarts the app that uses the value, and the page waits for it. The ThingsBoard token and the license key restart one app and take about thirty seconds. The Plate Recognizer API token restarts the add-on and Node-RED, which takes about a minute. Traffic isn't counted while Node-RED restarts.

An older device may have kept a token in `config.yml` or in the add-on's env file, or a Frigate+ key in `frigate.env`. The installer moves it to the device's secrets, so uploads, plate reads, and Frigate+ keep working, and the Device page and the Detection page show it as set. A warning on the Status page's ThingsBoard upload check says when `config.yml` still holds a token key, which nothing reads, or when the upload is on without a token.

### Download diagnostics

When you ask for help, send the diagnostics with your question. It's a text file with the device's facts, its date and time settings, every status check, the services' states, what the installer installed and found, and the last 50 lines of each service's log. Passwords, keys, tokens, and the setup code are replaced with `<redacted>`. The file names the device and holds its serial number.

- **Download diagnostics** saves the file.
- **Copy** puts the text on the clipboard, ready to paste into a message. If the browser doesn't allow it, the page shows the text in a box, already selected, for you to copy.

### Reboot or shut down

**Reboot the device** and **Shut down the device** each ask before they act. A reboot takes about two minutes, during which no page answers. If something such as a system update is holding the device up, or the control app isn't allowed to, the device says it can't reboot or shut down right now. Try again in a few minutes, and if it keeps happening, download the diagnostics.

Shut down only when you can reach the device

After a shutdown, nothing starts the device again from the network. To turn it back on, unplug its power and plug it back in.

## The Date and time page

The page shows two clocks side by side: **This device** and **This browser** (the phone or computer you're using), each with its date and offset from UTC. Under them, a sentence says whether they agree, or how far apart they are and whether their time zones differ.

- **Set from this browser** sends your browser's time and time zone to the device. If the device already has its time from the internet, it keeps that time, and only the time zone changes. Otherwise it takes your browser's time. If the device doesn't know your browser's time zone, which can happen when your phone or computer has a newer list of zones, it still takes the time, leaves its time zone as it was, and asks you to pick one from the list.
- **Time zone**: pick a zone, type part of its name to find it, then choose **Save time zone**. The installer sets the first time zone (its `-z` option, see [Installer options](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/reference/tmsetup/index.md)); this page changes it later. The dashboards show times, and start each day at 04:00, in the device's time zone.
- **Keep time from the internet** turns internet time on or off. The sentence under the switch says where the device's time comes from now.

Changing the time zone restarts Frigate, Node-RED, and the web proxy, so they all use the new zone. The page stops answering for a moment, and traffic isn't counted for about a minute.

Moving the clock ahead by more than about 20 seconds stops Frigate's camera feed, and a move of a few minutes can stop it until Frigate restarts. So when a change moves the clock ahead by that much, the device restarts Frigate and the page says so. Traffic isn't counted for about a minute. Moving the clock back restarts nothing, unless internet time briefly puts the device's later time back while it's being set, and then the page says so.

When the device has no internet

A Raspberry Pi keeps no time while it's off, unless it has a clock battery. A device without internet then starts with a clock that may be wrong. The Status page's **Clock** check shows a warning that no time source is reachable, or a problem if the date is before 2026. Open **Date and time** on your phone or computer and choose **Set from this browser**. The clock is usually behind after a power-off, so this moves it ahead and restarts Frigate; the camera is back in about a minute. Internet time stays on, so the device corrects its clock by itself once it's online; until then the warning stays. If the device's clock was ahead, turning internet time back on puts that wrong time back, so the device sets your time again, leaves internet time off, and the page says so. Turn on **Keep time from the internet** once the device is online. If that puts the wrong time back for a moment, the device restarts Frigate; the camera is back in about a minute. If a later correction stops the camera, the Status page offers **Restart Frigate**. A device that is never online keeps time from its own clock, which drifts; set it again now and then.

## What viewers see

Viewers see all five pages, but can't change anything:

- **Status**: the same checks, without the Restart and Re-scan buttons.
- **Device**: the card and the software versions, without **Tokens and keys**, **Diagnostics**, and **Power**.
- **Detection**: the models and the label lists, without the action buttons and the Frigate+ key form; see [Choose the detection model](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/detection/#the-detection-page).
- **Date and time**: the clocks, the time zone, and where the time comes from, without the button, the zone picker, or the switch.
- **Network**: the addresses and the hotspot's state, without the hotspot's password or any control.

______________________________________________________________________

## description: The device's home page and the apps it links to: dashboards, Frigate, Node-RED, camera feeds, and Cockpit.

# Home page and apps

Open `http://<device>/` in a browser on the same network. `<device>` is the hostname you set when you imaged the card, followed by `.local` (for example `http://tm-01.local/`), or the device's IP address.

The home page is the device's [control app](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/control-app/index.md). A new device first asks you to claim it with its setup code; after that, the home page and every app ask you to log in. The home page shows the device's name, software version, serial number, and time, a one-line summary of its health, and links to the apps your account can open. Its menu has **Status**, **Device**, and **Date and time** (see [Check and fix the device](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/device-health/index.md)), **Detection** (see [Choose the detection model](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/detection/index.md)), **Location** for administrators (see [Places and location](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/location/index.md)), your **Account**, the **Users** page for administrators, and **Log out**.

| Link             | Path                    | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Who can open it                                                                    |
| ---------------- | ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Dashboard        | `/dashboard/`           | The Traffic Monitor dashboards: [Monitoring](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/ui/monitoring/index.md), [Movements](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/ui/movements/index.md), and [Data export](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/ui/database/index.md), which opens first. Switch pages in the sidebar.                                                                                                                   | Any user. The Data export downloads need an administrator.                         |
| Frigate          | `/frigate/`             | Object detection: live view, detections with snapshots and clips, zones, masks, and the Frigate settings. See [Tune object detection](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/configuration/frigate-config/index.md).                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Any user. Frigate's settings need an administrator.                                |
| Legacy Dashboard | `/ui/`                  | The older dashboard, with the same counts and speed statistics as Monitoring. It's the only dashboard that shows [air quality](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/add-ons/air-quality/index.md) readings, and the Monitoring dashboard's counts follow its camera and radar selection. Its System Settings tab shows the device's name, time zone, and software versions, and holds the ThingsBoard Backup & Restore section. | Any user                                                                           |
| Node-RED editor  | `/nr/`                  | The flow editor, for developers. See [Dev environment](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/development/dev-environment/index.md).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Administrators                                                                     |
| Camera feeds     | `/feeds/`               | The camera streams the Pi camera produces, for checking that the camera works. It's for watching only: go2rtc's settings, stream editor, and log pages aren't available here.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Administrators                                                                     |
| Cockpit          | `http://<device>:9090/` | Services, logs, containers, and a terminal. See [System administration](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/system-admin/#cockpit).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Administrators see its link. Anyone with the Raspberry Pi user account can log in. |

Cockpit is the one app with its own port. It asks for the Raspberry Pi user account, not your control app login.

Finding the device's address

- If you set a hostname in Raspberry Pi Imager, `http://<hostname>.local/` works from most computers and phones on the same network.
- Otherwise, look the device up in your router's list of connected devices, or see [Find the IP address of your Raspberry Pi](https://www.raspberrypi.com/documentation/computers/remote-access.html#ip-address).
- A device whose Wi-Fi isn't on a network it knows runs its own hotspot. Join it, and your phone's sign-in window opens the home page; or open `http://10.42.0.1/`. See [Wi-Fi and the hotspot](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/wifi-hotspot/index.md).

If the home page doesn't load

Apart from Cockpit, the apps accept connections only from the device, so they have no address of their own on your network. If the apps show a page saying the control app isn't answering, restart it as described in [If the control app is down](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/control-app/#if-the-control-app-is-down). If nothing loads, open Cockpit at `http://<device>:9090`, log in with your Raspberry Pi user account, and check the services as described in [System administration](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/system-admin/index.md). [Network ports](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/reference/network/index.md) lists what the device opens. If the home page loads on a computer but times out on an Android phone, see [Troubleshooting](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/help-and-faq/frequently-asked-questions/#troubleshooting).

# Places and location

The control app's **Location** page records where the device is and which way its sensors face. It also sets how precisely the database stores the location. Only the administrator sees the page, because it shows exact coordinates. A device that stays in one place works without it, so use it when you move the device, turn it, or plan to share its data.

## Places and deployments

A *place* is somewhere the device has been, is, or will be. Each place has an id such as `3f9a1c2e-si`, an optional description that only you see, and an optional location, its latitude and longitude. A place doesn't need a location: a device with none still counts and records its data, only without saying where. One place can hold sensors that face different ways, such as a corner with a radar looking down each street.

One place is always **In use**. The others are **Planned**, entered ahead of a move, or **Used**, where the device has been. Claiming a new device creates its first place, **First location**, with no location.

Each sensor at a place, facing one way, for one stretch of time, is a *deployment*. Every count and reading is stored with its deployment, so you can tell where it was taken after the device moves. Moving to another place, or turning a sensor, starts a new deployment, and the earlier ones keep what they recorded.

The exact location is kept in the control app and in Node-RED's settings file, [`config.yml`](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/configuration/node-red-config/#deployment). The database stores the place's id and the location rounded to the [precision](#choose-the-precision) you choose.

## The Location page

**Location** is in the control app's menu, after **Detection**. The card at the top shows the place in use: its description, its id, the location as the database stores it, the exact location, whether the device shares its data with a [ThingsBoard](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/data-and-payloads/integrations/index.md) server, and the way each sensor faces. Then come the list of places and, last, the [precision](#choose-the-precision).

Each place in the list shows its description, or **No description**, its mark (**In use**, **Planned**, or **Used**), its id, and its location as the database stores it. Select a place to open it. An open place shows:

- **Imported from your previous settings** for a place that came from an older version's data; see [Update the software](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/build-your-own-device-diy/update/#places-after-an-update).
- When the place was first and last used, or **Not used yet**.
- How many events were recorded there, and between which dates.
- Its deployments, newest first, grouped by when they were deployed: the sensors started together sit under one date, each with the way it faced and **Correct bearing**. A radar deployed with a camera is indented under it. A sensor that ended before the rest of its group says when.
- The buttons for what you can do with the place: **Deploy here** for a planned place, **Re-deploy here** for a used one, or **Modify deployment** for the place in use; **Edit** for a planned place; **Correct location** for a used place or the place in use that has a location; and **Delete** for any place but the one in use.

**Before any place was recorded** counts the deployments that had already ended when the device got its first place. They belong to no place, and the database keeps them as they are. Deployments still running then joined that first place.

If Node-RED hasn't answered yet, as right after an update, a warning at the top says past places may be missing. Reload the page once Node-RED is running. Opening the control app's home page or Status page sets the places up too.

## Add a place

Choose **Add a place**, fill in what you know, and **Save**. The place is added as planned.

- **Description**: a name for the place, such as "Front of the school". It never leaves the device.
- **Coordinates**: the latitude and longitude, pasted from a maps app as one value, such as `45.52252, -122.69120`. Use a dot as the decimal mark. The device keeps five decimal places, about a metre. Leave the field empty for a place with no location.
- **Which way each sensor faces here**: `N`, `NE`, `E`, `SE`, `S`, `SW`, `W`, `NW`, or **Not set**, for each sensor turned on in the settings.

**Use this phone's location** fills in the coordinates from your phone's location. Browsers share a location only with pages opened over HTTPS, and the device uses plain HTTP, so the form usually says to paste coordinates instead.

To change a planned place, open it and choose **Edit**. A place that has been used can't be edited; [correct it](#correct-a-wrong-location-or-bearing) instead.

## Move or turn the device

When the device moves to another place, record it from that place: **Deploy here** if the place is planned, or **Re-deploy here** if the device has been there before. When a sensor is turned to face another way, record it with **Modify deployment** on the place in use.

1. Open the place, and choose its button.
1. Check the review. For each sensor, it says whether a new deployment starts, the way the sensor faced before, and the way it faces now, which you can change. Under the sensors are what the database will store for the place and whether the device shares its data.
1. Choose **Deploy**, **Re-deploy**, or **Modify**.

The page waits while Node-RED starts the new deployments, then lists their ids, each with **Copy**. Counts from then on belong to the new deployments.

In **Modify deployment**, the review starts with each sensor's bearing as it is, and each sensor reads **Unchanged** until you change its bearing. **Modify** stays off until at least one bearing changes, and only the sensors you turned start a new deployment.

Don't deploy twice

If Node-RED hasn't loaded the new settings within about 20 seconds, the page says the settings are saved and the deployments appear once Node-RED loads them. If the connection drops while the page waits, it says the settings may already be saved. In both cases, close the dialog and check the place in the list before you deploy again.

A move usually also needs the camera's zones adjusted; see [First-time setup](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/setup-guide/#3-adjust-the-zones).

## Correct a wrong location or bearing

A correction is for a value that was entered wrong. It changes what the records already say, and starts no new deployment. If the device moved or was turned, [record that](#move-or-turn-the-device) instead.

- **Correct location**, on a used place or the place in use, takes a new latitude and longitude. Every record from the place then says it was at the new point, rounded to the precision each was stored at. For the place in use, `config.yml` takes the new point too. A point more than about 1 km from the old one looks like a move, so the page asks a second time and gives the distance. A place with no location can't be corrected to one: add a new place with the location, and deploy it.
- **Correct bearing**, on each deployment in an open place, takes the way the sensor really faced. Every record from that deployment then says so. For a deployment that is still running, `config.yml` takes the new bearing too.

Each correction can have a **Reason**, which is kept with the correction on the device. Copies of the database already downloaded, and data already uploaded, keep the old values.

## Import places from a file

To plan several places at once, choose **Import places**. Pick a CSV file, or paste its lines into the box.

- The first line is the header. It starts with `description,lat,lon`, then has one column for each sensor turned on in the settings, named as in the settings. The dialog shows this device's header.
- Each further line is one place. Leave `lat` and `lon` both empty for a place with no location. A sensor's column holds the way it faces, `n`, `ne`, `e`, `se`, `s`, `sw`, `w`, or `nw`, or nothing.
- A file can be up to 64 KiB.

For a device with the Pi camera and one radar:

```
description,lat,lon,picam_h265,TM_RADAR_SERIAL_PORT_00
Front of the school,45.52252,-122.69120,n,n
Corner by the park,,,e,e
```

Choose **Preview** to see the places the file holds and, by line number, any lines with a problem. **Import** adds the places as planned. It's offered only when every line can be read, and it adds all of them or none.

## Delete a place

Open the place and choose **Delete**, then confirm. A planned place is removed from the list. A used place's exact location is deleted with it, and the database keeps the rounded location stored with each of its records. Deleting can't be undone.

The place in use can't be deleted. Deploy another place first.

## Choose the precision

**Precision**, at the end of the page, sets how much of the location the database stores. To better protect your privacy, it's rounded to about 1 km by default. The choices stay closed until you open **Change the precision**, which also shows the current choice, because most devices never need to change it. The setting is for the whole device, not for one place. Each choice shows how the same point would be stored:

| Choice                                       | The database stores                      |
| -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| **No location stored**                       | No coordinates                           |
| **About 10 km** (45.5, -122.7)               | One decimal place, about a city          |
| **About 1 km** (45.52, -122.69), the default | Two decimal places, about a neighborhood |

The exact location is never stored in the database. It stays on this device, and a later update will let you choose to export the database with each place's exact location, for analysis and mapping. Choose one and **Save**.

- **A coarser choice** applies to the deployments running now at once. Rows stored before them keep their precision unless you tick **Also round the rows already stored**, which asks first, because it can't be undone.
- **No location stored** removes the stored location from the deployments running now at once. Tick **Also remove it from the rows already stored** to remove it from every row in the database as well, which also asks first. The exact location stays on the device, but the database can't get the rounded values back.
- **A finer choice** applies from the next deployment. Rows already stored stay as they are, because what was rounded away can't come back.

## What leaves the device

- A place's description, and the reasons you give for corrections, never leave the device.
- A copy of the database holds the place's id and its location at the stored precision: about a neighborhood at about 1 km, or about a city at about 10 km. The exact location isn't in it.
- A correction or a coarser precision changes the device's own records only. Copies of the database already downloaded, and data already uploaded, keep the values they had.

To change these values in `config.yml` by hand, see [Edit the location by hand](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/configuration/node-red-config/#edit-the-location-by-hand).

# System administration

## Cockpit

[Cockpit](https://cockpit-project.org/) is the device's system console in the browser. It shows the services and their logs, the Podman containers, system updates, and the user accounts, and it has a terminal, so most administration needs no SSH client.

Open `http://<device>:9090/`, with the same name or address you use for the home page, and log in with your Raspberry Pi user account. Administrators also have a **Cockpit** tile on the home page, which opens the same address and names the account to log in with.

Cockpit has its own port and its own login. It doesn't need the home page, the [control app](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/control-app/index.md), or the apps, so it still opens when they don't. Use it when:

- the home page doesn't load, or a page says the control app isn't answering
- you want to restart a service, or read its log
- you need a terminal and have no SSH client
- you want to install system updates or change the system password

Who can open Cockpit

Anyone on your network can reach Cockpit's login page. Only the Raspberry Pi user account gets past it. The control app's accounts don't work there.

## Services

The Traffic Monitor runs as systemd services. The app containers run inside one Podman pod. nginx and the control app run on the host, outside the pod, so the home page and the login stay up when the pod is down.

Start with the control app's [Status page](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/device-health/#the-status-page): it shows each service's state, and when one has stopped or keeps failing, its check has a **Restart** button. Use Cockpit or SSH for the rest, such as restarting the control app itself, or a service that looks running but misbehaves.

| Service                    | What it runs                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `traffic-monitor.service`  | The pod that holds Frigate, Node-RED, and Plate Recognizer if installed                                                                                                                                        |
| `frigate.service`          | Frigate, object detection                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `node-red-tm.service`      | Node-RED: the Traffic Monitor logic, dashboards, database, and MQTT broker                                                                                                                                     |
| `tm-control.service`       | The [control app](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/control-app/index.md): the home page's data, the login, the device's accounts, and the status checks. nginx asks it to check the login for every app. |
| `revproxy.service`         | nginx, which serves the home page and the `/dashboard/`, `/frigate/`, and other paths                                                                                                                          |
| `plate-recognizer.service` | The optional [Plate Recognizer](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/add-ons/plate-recognizer/index.md) add-on                                                                                                   |
| `go2rtc_server.service`    | go2rtc, which reads the Pi camera and streams it to Frigate. It runs on the host, not in the pod.                                                                                                              |

Over SSH:

```
sudo systemctl status traffic-monitor.service   # or any service above
sudo systemctl restart node-red-tm.service      # after editing node-red-tm.env
sudo journalctl -u frigate.service -f           # follow a service's log
sudo podman ps                                  # running containers
```

## When to restart what

| After you                                         | Do this                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Edit Node-RED's `config.yml`                      | Nothing. The Traffic Monitor reads the file again when you save it. If the change doesn't show, check the file for a YAML error. For the location, use the control app's [Location page](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/location/index.md) instead; [Edit the location by hand](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/configuration/node-red-config/#edit-the-location-by-hand) says what a hand edit does. |
| Edit `node-red-tm.env`                            | `sudo systemctl restart node-red-tm.service`. The container reads the file only when it starts.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Edit `frigate.env`                                | `sudo systemctl restart frigate.service`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Change the MQTT broker login in `node-red-tm.env` | `bash traffic-monitor/script/tmsetup.sh -t node-red-tm`. A restart isn't enough; [Env file settings](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/configuration/environment/#node-red-tmenv) explains why.                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Change Frigate's config in its UI                 | Choose **Save & Restart** in Frigate's config editor, or restart `frigate.service`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Plug in a radar                                   | Rerun the installer for Node-RED so the radar is passed to the container: `bash traffic-monitor/script/tmsetup.sh -t node-red-tm`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Add or change an AI accelerator                   | Rerun the installer with `-t detectors -t frigate`, then update Frigate's detector settings. See [Add an accelerator later](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/reference/tmsetup/#add-an-accelerator-later).                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| See a page saying the control app isn't answering | `sudo systemctl restart tm-control.service`, or restart it in Cockpit on port 9090. See [If the control app is down](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/control-app/#if-the-control-app-is-down).                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Move the device to a new site                     | Choose **Deploy here** on the new place on the [Location page](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/location/#move-or-turn-the-device), then adjust the zones as in [First-time setup](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/setup-guide/#3-adjust-the-zones).                                                                                                                                                    |

## The device's card

`sudo tm-control card` prints the device's address, the name and password of its [hotspot](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/wifi-hotspot/index.md), and its setup code while it's unclaimed. It needs `sudo` because the code is in a file only root can read, and the password in a file only root and the installing user's group can. `sudo tm-control card --json` prints the same values as JSON. If you lose the administrator's password, `sudo tm-control reset-admin` starts the accounts over; see [If the administrator's password is lost](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/control-app/#if-the-administrators-password-is-lost).

## Where things are

The settings and data live under `/opt/traffic-monitor/`.

| Path                                    | Contents                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `node-red-tm/config/config.yml`         | Traffic Monitor settings. See [config.yml settings](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/configuration/node-red-config/index.md).                                                                                                                                                      |
| `node-red-tm/node-red-tm.env`           | Radar ports, database path, MQTT broker. See [Env file settings](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/configuration/environment/#node-red-tmenv).                                                                                                                                      |
| `node-red-tm/db/tmdb.sqlite`            | The database. `db/backup/` holds the copy saved before the most recent schema change. After the upgrade that rounded the stored coordinates, that copy still has the exact ones, so don't share it.                                                                                  |
| `frigate/config/config.yml`             | Frigate's settings, including zones and masks.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `frigate/config/model_cache/`           | The models Frigate runs, such as a [Frigate+](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/configuration/frigate-config/#better-models) model's two files. The control app's [Detection page](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/detection/index.md) uploads, downloads, and deletes them. |
| `frigate/frigate.env`                   | Frigate's environment, including the Frigate+ API key, which comes from the device's secrets. See [Env file settings](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/configuration/environment/#frigateenv).                                                                                     |
| `frigate/storage/`                      | Frigate's snapshots and recordings.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `plate-recognizer/plate-recognizer.env` | Plate Recognizer settings, if the add-on is installed. Its token and license key come from the device's secrets, which you set on the [Device page](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/device-health/#tokens-and-keys).                                                          |

The control app and the installer keep a few files elsewhere. Read them, but don't edit them.

| Path                                 | Contents                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/var/lib/tm-control/state.sqlite`   | The control app's accounts, the license acceptance, and a log of account changes. Only the control app writes it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `/etc/traffic-monitor/manifest.json` | What the installer installed and found, which the control app reads                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `/etc/traffic-monitor/secrets/`      | Passwords and keys the installer generated on the device, including the hotspot's password, which administrators can show on the [Network page](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/wifi-hotspot/#show-the-password), and the tokens and keys you enter on the [Device page](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/device-health/#tokens-and-keys) and the [Detection page](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/detection/#frigate-plus) |
| `/etc/traffic-monitor/setup-code`    | The setup code, until the device is claimed                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

# Wi-Fi and the hotspot

When a Traffic Monitor's Wi-Fi isn't on a network it knows, the unit runs a hotspot of its own. The hotspot is how you reach a unit at the roadside, where there's no router. It runs whether or not the unit is also on Ethernet.

The hotspot's name is `TM-` and four characters from the unit's serial number, such as `TM-4F2A`, until an administrator [renames it](#rename-the-hotspot). It uses WPA2 on the 2.4 GHz band. The [Status page](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/device-health/#the-status-page) shows its state.

## Join the hotspot

1. Find the hotspot's name and password on the unit's card. The card is the printout that came with a pre-built unit; for a unit you installed yourself, the installer shows it at the end of its run on the device. An administrator can also show the password on the [Network page](#the-network-page), and `sudo tm-control card` on the unit prints it again, together with the setup code while the unit is [unclaimed](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/control-app/#claim-the-device).
1. On your phone, join the hotspot with that password. Your phone may say the network has no internet. Stay connected.
1. The phone's sign-in window opens the control app by itself, on its login or setup page. If it doesn't, open `http://10.42.0.1/` in a browser. The unit's `.local` name, `http://<hostname>.local/`, also works.

The hotspot has no internet, and a phone on it reaches only the unit. Nothing on the unit's Ethernet or home network is reachable from the hotspot.

### Phones

- **Android 17:** the sign-in window is the way in. Android 17 browsers can't open the unit while the phone is on its hotspot, so don't close the window until you're done. See [the Android 17 entry](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/help-and-faq/frequently-asked-questions/#troubleshooting) if the page doesn't open on your home network either.
  - The database and JSON downloads on the [Data export page](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/ui/database/index.md) save from the sign-in window. The unit prepares the database twice there, once for the window and once for the phone's downloader, so the wait before a database download starts is about double.
  - **Download diagnostics** on the Device page doesn't save from the sign-in window: the phone says "Could not download". Download it from a computer on the unit's network instead.
  - Frigate's downloads, such as a snapshot, don't save from the sign-in window either.
- **iPhone:** to stay on the hotspot and save downloads, tap **Cancel** on the sign-in sheet and choose **Use Without Internet**. Then open `http://10.42.0.1/` or the unit's `.local` name in a browser. The login and setup pages show that name while the phone is on the hotspot. Without that choice the iPhone goes back to another network it knows, and a download in progress is cut off. The sign-in sheet itself shows a downloaded file's contents instead of saving it.

Tested with a Pixel 7 on Android 17 and with Firefox on an iPhone on iOS 18.7, in November 2026.

## The Network page

**Network** in the [control app](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/control-app/index.md)'s menu shows how to reach the unit and what it is connected to. Everyone who is signed in sees:

- **This device:** the unit's name and its `.local` name, such as `tm-ab12` and `tm-ab12.local`.
- **Ethernet** and **Wi-Fi:** whether each is connected, and for each its MAC address, IP address, gateway, and DNS servers. The Wi-Fi line says which network the unit is on, with its signal, or that it is on its own hotspot. A unit without Ethernet has no Ethernet line, and a unit without a built-in radio says so.
- **Internet:** whether the unit reaches the internet. An offline unit says **Not reachable**, which is normal.
- **Hotspot:** whether it is on, its name, whether the name is hidden, and the two addresses it answers on.
- **Wi-Fi networks:** the networks the unit has saved and the ones it heard the last time it looked. See [Put the unit on a Wi-Fi network](#put-the-unit-on-a-wi-fi-network) and [Saved networks](#saved-networks).

**This device** and **Hotspot** sit side by side on a wide screen, above **Wi-Fi networks**, and are folded each time you open the page. Folded, **This device** shows the `.local` name and the addresses in use, and **Hotspot** shows its name, or **Hotspot off**. Select a heading to open it. A panel opens by itself when something in it needs your attention, such as a hotspot change that fails or is refused, and a folded one then shows a warning mark.

Every name and address has a **Copy** button. If the network service doesn't answer, the page says so and shows only the names.

The [Device page](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/device-health/#the-device-page) shows the same addresses in a short summary, with a link to this page.

Find the MAC address

A router set to admit listed devices only needs the unit's Wi-Fi **MAC address**. Open **This device** on the Network page, copy the address from the Wi-Fi block, and add it to the router's list.

Viewers see the lists of networks, a join's progress card (read only, with no buttons), the hotspot's state, name, whether the name is hidden, and addresses, and nothing else. They never see its password or a control. Administrators get the controls described in the rest of this page: put the unit on a Wi-Fi network, change the saved networks, show or change the hotspot's password, rename the hotspot, hide its name, and turn it on or off.

Changes restart the hotspot

A change to the hotspot's name, password, or hidden setting restarts it when it is up. Phones on it are disconnected, and each phone must rejoin by hand. When you use the Network page from a phone on the hotspot, the page stops answering when you save. Join the hotspot again, then reload the page. The page warns you before a change that restarts the hotspot, before you turn the hotspot off, and before you hide its name. Turning the hotspot on doesn't ask.

## Put the unit on a Wi-Fi network

An administrator can put the unit on a Wi-Fi network from the Network page, without a cable or a keyboard. The unit tests the network first, and switches to it only once the test has passed and the countdown has ended or you choose **Switch now**.

1. Open **Network**. Under **Wi-Fi networks**, choose **Refresh** to have the unit look for networks. It takes about 4 seconds, and a phone on the hotspot pauses for a few seconds while the unit looks. **Nearby networks** lists what it heard, strongest first, and says how long ago it looked.
1. Choose **Join** next to the network, and read what the dialog says will happen. It shows the unit's Wi-Fi MAC address too.
1. Type the network's password, and choose **Test and join**. The page shows the password as you type it, and asks only once.

The unit doesn't save the network or its password at this point. Until the switch, the network exists only in the unit's memory, so a wrong password never reaches the microSD card.

### The test

A test takes up to about a minute, and the unit's radio is busy with it. If the unit was on its hotspot, the hotspot is away for the test and a phone on it is disconnected. The hotspot is back within a few seconds after the test ends. Join it again by hand, and reload the page to see the result. If the unit was on another network, it leaves that network for the test and returns to it. Until the join ends (the test, the countdown, and the switch), the unit refuses every other Wi-Fi or hotspot change. Once the test has passed, choose **Cancel** or **Switch now** to free it.

The test asks the network for an address, then asks the network's DNS server for the address of `connectivity-check.ubuntu.com` (up to three times, a second apart, because the first question right after joining can fail) and makes one request to it, to see whether the internet is reachable. The unit comes back to where it was either way. To test a network the unit has saved already, choose **Join** and keep its saved password, or enter a new one.

A card at the top of the Network page shows the test as it runs. Administrators also see a line with a **See it** link on the [home page](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/home-page/index.md), so you can find the result from there.

### The result and the countdown

When the test passes, the card says **`<name>` works** and shows:

- the address the unit got on that network, and its `.local` name, which you can use to reach it there;
- the unit's Wi-Fi MAC address;
- whether the internet is reachable there.

Below that, a countdown starts at 5 minutes: **Joining `<name>` in 4:32**. Use the time to join the same network with your phone or computer, so you can open one of the addresses once the unit has switched.

- **Switch now** ends the countdown, and the unit joins at once.
- **Cancel** ends it, and the unit stays where it is. Nothing is saved.
- If you do nothing, the unit joins when the countdown ends.

When the unit joins, the network is saved and the unit uses it. If the unit was on the hotspot, the hotspot stops. A phone on the hotspot loses it, so join the network yourself and open one of the addresses from the card. On an Android 17 phone a browser may not open a device on the phone's own Wi-Fi network; see [the Android 17 entry](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/help-and-faq/frequently-asked-questions/#troubleshooting) if the address doesn't open. The result stays on the page until you choose **Dismiss**.

A network with a sign-in page

Some networks, such as a hotel's or a cafe's, give the unit an address but make a device open a web page before it reaches the internet. The unit can't complete that page. The card says "Joined, but this network needs a sign-in page, so the unit has no internet there." The unit can still join the network and be reached on it, and you can switch to it if you want that.

### If the test fails

The card says why, and the unit is back where it was. Nothing is saved for a new network.

| The card says                                                                     | What it means                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **`<name>` isn't in range right now, so nothing was tried**                       | The unit didn't hear the network when it checked, so it left its radio alone. Choose **Refresh** and try again from a place with a better signal.                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **The unit couldn't join `<name>`**                                               | Usually a wrong password. This fails after about 25 seconds. A router set to admit listed devices only also refuses the unit until you add the unit's Wi-Fi MAC address, which the card and the dialog show, to its list.                                                                                                                    |
| **`<name>` let the unit in but gave it no address**                               | The unit connected, but the network's DHCP gave it nothing. This fails after about 45 seconds. Try again later, or check the network's address range.                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **The unit was busy with its Wi-Fi**                                              | Another Wi-Fi change was under way. Try again in a minute.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **The test couldn't run**                                                         | The unit couldn't prepare to come back, so it left its radio alone, or it hit an error it didn't expect. It is back where it was.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **The test of `<name>` was interrupted**                                          | The test stopped partway, for example because the unit lost power. The unit goes back to where it was within a minute and a half.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **The test passed, but the unit couldn't join `<name>` when the countdown ended** | The unit is back where it was. If the network went away during the countdown, the switch waits for it, and the hotspot is away for up to about a minute before it comes back. The network stays saved, and the unit tries it again by itself, after a wait that grows to about an hour. See [When the hotspot runs](#when-the-hotspot-runs). |

A saved network that fails is kept, because the cause may be temporary. A new network that fails is not saved.

## Saved networks

**Saved networks** lists the networks the unit joins by itself. Above the list the page says: "The unit joins the first of these it finds." The order is the order the unit tries them in, so the network at the top wins when more than one is in range. A network the unit joined from the page goes to the top of the list.

Each network shows whether it is **Joined**, **In range**, or **Not in range**, and flags a network that is **Hidden** or **Not joined by itself**. A network saved through Raspberry Pi Imager's Wi-Fi settings shows here too, as an ordinary saved network.

- **Move up** and **Move down** change a network's place in the order. Only the networks the unit joins by itself have a place.
- **Forget** deletes a saved network, after a question. The unit no longer joins it. When it isn't the network in use, nothing else changes.
- **Forget** on the network in use makes the unit leave it. The question says so, and says what happens next. The hotspot starts within about 5 seconds, and a page opened over that network loses the unit, so join the hotspot and open `http://10.42.0.1/`. With the hotspot turned off, the question warns that the unit then has no wireless way in, and that you would need an Ethernet cable.

### Couldn't join

A saved network that the unit failed to join shows **Couldn't join**. The unit tries again by itself, about 10 minutes after the failure, then about 20, then about 65 minutes after each further one; [When the hotspot runs](#when-the-hotspot-runs) has the details. Joining the network by hand from the page, with the right password, tests it again at once.

## When the hotspot runs

The hotspot yields to the networks the unit has saved. A unit joins a saved network that's in range, and the hotspot runs when none is.

| Situation                                      | What happens                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The unit starts with a saved network in range  | It's on the network within a minute. The hotspot stays off.                                                                                                                            |
| The unit starts with no saved network in range | The hotspot is up about 15 seconds after the unit starts.                                                                                                                              |
| The unit's Wi-Fi network disappears            | The hotspot starts about 75 seconds later.                                                                                                                                             |
| A saved network has the wrong password         | The hotspot is away for about a minute while the unit tries the network, then comes back.                                                                                              |
| You join a network from the page               | The hotspot is away for up to a minute for the test, then comes back. When the countdown ends, or you choose **Switch now**, the unit joins the network and the hotspot stops at once. |
| You forget the network in use                  | The hotspot starts within about 5 seconds.                                                                                                                                             |

While the hotspot is up and nobody is joined to it, the unit looks for its saved networks every 5 minutes and joins one it hears. A network that won't join is tried again about 10 minutes after the failure, then about 20 minutes after the next one, then about 65 minutes after each further failure. While a phone is joined to the hotspot, the unit doesn't look, so nothing interrupts the phone.

The Status page's Hotspot check says which of these the unit is in, and its **Restart the hotspot** button has the unit look at its radio at once.

### Turn the hotspot off

1. Sign in as an administrator and open **Network**.
1. Under **Hotspot**, switch off **Hotspot on**.
1. Read the warning, and choose **Turn off** if you still want to.
