- `/opt/traffic-monitor/node-red-tm/config/config.yml`
- `/opt/traffic-monitor/node-red-tm/node-red-tm.env`
- `/opt/traffic-monitor/frigate/config/config.yml`, which holds zones and masks drawn in Frigate
- `/opt/traffic-monitor/frigate/frigate.env`. Its Frigate+ key comes from the device's secrets.
- `/opt/traffic-monitor/plate-recognizer/plate-recognizer.env`, if Plate Recognizer is installed. Its token and license key come from the device's secrets.

With `-f`, each is replaced by a fresh copy from its template, and the old file stays next to it with a timestamp in its name so you can copy your settings back. The MQTT broker login carries into the fresh `node-red-tm.env` and `frigate.env`. A fresh Frigate config has detection off and the sample zones, so afterwards turn detection on and redo your zones and masks, as in [First-time setup](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/setup-guide/index.md).

The fresh Frigate config keeps one thing from the old one: the `model:` section, if you chose a model, whether in Frigate's model picker, its configuration editor, or by hand (see [Better models](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/configuration/frigate-config/#better-models)). It's kept even when Frigate can't load that model; see [If Frigate stops over a model](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/configuration/frigate-config/#if-frigate-stops-over-a-model). The installer's own model section for a Coral isn't kept, so the fresh copy gets the model for the accelerator the installer finds. Comments inside a kept section are lost; its keys keep their order. If the old config isn't valid YAML, the fresh copy gets the installer's model section, and the installer says so.

No run, with or without `-f`, replaces the device's accounts, its setup code, or the passwords and keys in `/etc/traffic-monitor/secrets/`, including the ThingsBoard token, the Frigate+ API key, and the Plate Recognizer token and license key you entered. The installer writes those values into `node-red-tm.env`, `frigate.env`, and `plate-recognizer.env` on every run, so a fresh copy from `-f` has them too. The installer takes no secret value as an option: enter them on the [Device page](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/device-health/#tokens-and-keys), or the Frigate+ key on the [Detection page](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/detection/#frigate-plus).

## Add an accelerator later

After you add or change a Coral or Hailo accelerator, rerun two tags and reboot when the installer asks:

```
bash traffic-monitor/script/tmsetup.sh -t detectors -t frigate
```

That installs the driver and gives Frigate's container the device. Frigate's own `config.yml` still names the old detector, because the installer writes its `detectors:` and `model:` sections only when it creates the file. Either edit those two sections by hand to match the [template](https://github.com/glossyio/traffic-monitor/blob/main/container/frigate/config/config.yml.j2), or add `-f` to the command above and then redo your Frigate settings, as [What `-f` replaces](#what-f-replaces) describes.

`-f` keeps a model you chose, such as a Frigate+ model, and that model may not suit the new accelerator. If it doesn't, Frigate can't use it and counts nothing, and the Status page reports the problem. Pick a model built for the new accelerator (see [Use a model](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/configuration/frigate-config/#use-a-model)), or, to get the installer's model for it, delete the `model:` section in Frigate's configuration editor before you run the installer with `-f`.

## Reboots

The installer edits the boot configuration and installs kernel drivers, so it asks to reboot when needed. On the device, it prompts, and with `-y` it doesn't ask. Either way the reboot starts one minute later. Remote devices reboot by themselves. Services stay stopped until the reboot.

# Air quality

The optional [air quality sensor](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/add-ons/air-quality/index.md) publishes a reading over MQTT every five minutes. The Traffic Monitor stores each reading as a row in the `airquality` table.

## MQTT payload

The sensor software publishes to `aq/<sensor>/readings`, where `<sensor>` is the sensor's name in [config.yml](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/configuration/node-red-config/#sensorsairquality_monitors). Readings are dropped unless that sensor is enabled there.

```
{
    "gas_calibrated": false,
    "bar": [1009.44, "0"],
    "hum": [28.7, "2"],
    "pm025": 0,
    "pm10": 0,
    "pm01": 0,
    "dew": 2.1,
    "temp": 21,
    "temp_min": 20.9,
    "temp_max": 21.1,
    "gas_red": 4.2,
    "gas_oxi": 0.15,
    "gas_nh3": 0.69,
    "lux": 1.2,
    "proximity": 255,
    "lux_raw": 1.16185,
    "temp_raw": 28.68982029794099,
    "bar_raw": 1003.7122773175154,
    "hum_raw": 18.31337919009301,
    "gas_red_raw": 140805,
    "gas_oxi_raw": 103585,
    "gas_nh3_raw": 227871,
    "current_time": 1738698665.077546
}
```

`bar` and `hum` are pairs: the value, then a comfort-level code (`"0"` stable to `"4"` storm for pressure; `"1"` good, `"2"` dry, `"3"` wet for humidity). Only the value is stored. `temp_min`, `temp_max`, and the sensor software's `Forecast` object aren't stored. The sensor software's [README](https://github.com/greendormer/enviroplus-monitor) explains how it compensates and calibrates the readings.

## airquality table

| Column           | Type    | Meaning                                                                                                                   | Unit                 |
| ---------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- |
| `entryDateTime`  | REAL    | When the reading was taken (`current_time` in the payload)                                                                | Unix time in seconds |
| `gas_calibrated` | INTEGER | Whether the gas sensor had finished warming up, which takes about 100 minutes after the sensor software starts            | `1` yes, `0` no      |
| `temp`           | REAL    | Temperature, compensated for the heat of the device                                                                       | °C                   |
| `bar`            | REAL    | Air pressure, compensated for altitude                                                                                    | hPa                  |
| `hum`            | REAL    | Relative humidity, compensated                                                                                            | %                    |
| `dew`            | REAL    | Dew point, calculated from temperature and humidity                                                                       | °C                   |
| `temp_raw`       | REAL    | Temperature as measured                                                                                                   | °C                   |
| `bar_raw`        | REAL    | Air pressure as measured                                                                                                  | hPa                  |
| `hum_raw`        | REAL    | Relative humidity as measured                                                                                             | %                    |
| `pm01`           | REAL    | Particulate matter up to 1 µm                                                                                             | µg/m³                |
| `pm025`          | REAL    | Particulate matter up to 2.5 µm                                                                                           | µg/m³                |
| `pm10`           | REAL    | Particulate matter up to 10 µm                                                                                            | µg/m³                |
| `gas_red`        | REAL    | Reducing gases, such as carbon monoxide and hydrogen, compensated for drift                                               | ppm                  |
| `gas_oxi`        | REAL    | Oxidizing gases, such as nitrogen dioxide and chlorine, compensated for drift                                             | ppm                  |
| `gas_nh3`        | REAL    | Ammonia, compensated for drift                                                                                            | ppm                  |
| `gas_red_raw`    | REAL    | Reducing gas sensor resistance as measured                                                                                | Ω                    |
| `gas_oxi_raw`    | REAL    | Oxidizing gas sensor resistance as measured                                                                               | Ω                    |
| `gas_nh3_raw`    | REAL    | Ammonia sensor resistance as measured                                                                                     | Ω                    |
| `lux`            | REAL    | Light, with a proximity-adjusted minimum                                                                                  | lux                  |
| `lux_raw`        | REAL    | Light as measured                                                                                                         | lux                  |
| `proximity`      | REAL    | Proximity sensor reading; high when something is close to the board                                                       | 0 to 255             |
| `sensorName`     | TEXT    | The sensor's name                                                                                                         |                      |
| `deployment_id`  | TEXT    | The [deployment](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/data-and-payloads/data-overview/#deployment) the reading was taken in |                      |

## The sensors on the board

| Reading                         | Sensor                                                                                                                | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Gases                           | [MiCS-6814](https://www.sgxsensortech.com/content/uploads/2015/02/1143_Datasheet-MiCS-6814-rev-8.pdf)                 | Measures resistance for reducing, oxidizing, and ammonia gases. The sensor software converts resistance to ppm, compensating for temperature, humidity, and pressure, and recalibrates daily for drift. Treat the ppm values as relative; see the discussion in [pimoroni/enviroplus-python #47](https://github.com/pimoroni/enviroplus-python/issues/47) and [#67](https://github.com/pimoroni/enviroplus-python/issues/67). |
| Temperature, pressure, humidity | [BME280](https://www.bosch-sensortec.com/media/boschsensortec/downloads/datasheets/bst-bme280-ds002.pdf)              | The Raspberry Pi and AI accelerator warm the enclosure, so the compensated values are the ones to use. Pressure updates every 20 minutes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Light and proximity             | [LTR-559](https://optoelectronics.liteon.com/upload/download/DS86-2013-0003/LTR-559ALS-01_DS_V1.pdf)                  |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Noise                           | [SPH0645 MEMS microphone](https://media.digikey.com/pdf/Data%20Sheets/Knowles%20Acoustics%20PDFs/SPH0645LM4H-B.pdf)   | Not stored in the database                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Particulate matter              | Plantower [PMS5003](http://www.aqmd.gov/docs/default-source/aq-spec/resources-page/plantower-pms5003-manual_v2-3.pdf) |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

# Data and privacy

The Traffic Monitor is a data collection tool. Everything it collects is processed and stored on the device, in open formats, so you own it and can share it.

## What the device stores

| Where                                             | What                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | How long                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/opt/traffic-monitor/node-red-tm/db/tmdb.sqlite` | The database: [events](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/data-and-payloads/events-payload/index.md), [radar readings](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/data-and-payloads/radar-payload/index.md), [air quality readings](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/data-and-payloads/air-quality-aq-payload/index.md), the device's deployment history, and operator comments | Until you delete it                                                                                                     |
| `/opt/traffic-monitor/frigate/storage/`           | Frigate's cropped snapshots of each detection, and recordings of alerts and detections                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | About an hour, by default                                                                                               |
| Your ThingsBoard server                           | A copy of the data above, plus system metrics                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | If you turn on the [ThingsBoard upload](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/data-and-payloads/integrations/#thingsboard) |

## Privacy

We believe in [open data](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_data): anonymized data is a public good and the basis of useful research. The database is designed to be shareable. With the default settings it is [de-identified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De-identification): it records what passed (a label), when, how fast, and through which zones, and never an image or a plate number. Its location is rounded to about 1 km, which in a town shows the neighbourhood but not the address.

Images do exist on the device, briefly. Frigate keeps snapshots and short clips for about an hour so you can check what it detected. To keep none, turn off recordings and snapshots as described in [Tune object detection](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/configuration/frigate-config/#recordings-and-snapshots). To keep them longer, raise the retention there, and treat the device as holding images of people.

By default, the device sends no images or video anywhere. Everything is processed on the device, and `tmdb.sqlite` holds only metadata. The live view and the recordings are behind the device's [login](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/control-app/index.md), which decides who on your network can open the apps. It isn't a control on the images themselves: anyone with an account on the device can see them, and they're ordinary files on the device's card. Frigate can also publish a snapshot of each detected object on the device's [MQTT broker](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/data-and-payloads/integrations/#mqtt). New installs turn those snapshots off, and they stay on the device unless you give the broker a login, which opens it to your network. [Tune object detection](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/configuration/frigate-config/#recordings-and-snapshots) shows the setting. A snapshot you choose to [submit to Frigate+](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/configuration/frigate-config/#submit-snapshots) does leave the device, and it can show people.

With the default settings, the database is de-identified: it holds no images, plate numbers, or exact location. The place the device was used at is stored as a survey id, which has no coordinates in it, and any coordinates are rounded to about 1 km by default and never stored more precisely (see [deployment](#deployment)). Where homes are far apart, a square about 1 km across may hold only one or two of them, so the rounded location can point to the house even though it isn't exact. If the device is at a home, especially in a rural area, choose **About 10 km** or **No location stored** on the [Location](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/location/index.md) page before it starts recording. The exact location stays on the device, in `config.yml` and in the control app's list of places, and neither is part of the database.

The database stops being de-identified if you:

- Install the [Plate Recognizer](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/add-ons/plate-recognizer/index.md) add-on. Plate numbers go into the `plate_recognizer` table. Don't share a database from a device that has ever had the add-on on.
- Turn on Frigate features that add identifying sub-labels or attributes to events, such as face recognition or license plate recognition.
- Write identifying details into operator comments.
- Keep the copy of the database that an upgrade leaves in `db/backup/`. It can hold the exact coordinates from before they were rounded (see [deployment](#deployment)), so don't share it.

For an area the camera shouldn't see at all, such as a window or a yard, aim the camera so the area is out of frame. A [motion mask](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/configuration/frigate-config/#masks) only stops motion there from starting a detection; the area still shows in the live view and in recordings.

Other software on the device, such as Frigate and the air quality sensor's service, keeps its own working data under its own retention rules.

## Tables

Tables for sensors the device doesn't have stay empty.

| Table                              | Contents                                                                                                                                                      | Could identify a person?                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `events`                           | One row per object the camera detected, with direction and speed. See [Events](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/data-and-payloads/events-payload/index.md). | Only through Frigate sub-labels or attributes, if you turn those on                                                                                                                                                     |
| `radar_dov`                        | Detected object velocity readings from the radar                                                                                                              | No                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `radar_timed_speed_counts`         | Counts and average speeds the radar reports every 300 seconds                                                                                                 | No                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `radar_raw_speed_magnitude`        | Raw speed and magnitude readings, three per sample                                                                                                            | No                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `radar_raw_speed_magnitude_single` | The strongest reading of each sample                                                                                                                          | No                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `radar_oc_payload`                 | Per-object summaries from the radar, including estimated length                                                                                               | No                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `airquality`                       | Air quality and weather readings. See [Air quality](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/data-and-payloads/air-quality-aq-payload/index.md).                    | No                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `deployment`                       | Where each sensor was, and when                                                                                                                               | No, except where homes are far apart: the location is rounded to about 1 km (two decimal places) by default and never stored more precisely, which in a rural area can point to a single home (see [Privacy](#privacy)) |
| `comments`                         | Notes typed on the [Data export](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/ui/database/index.md) page                                                                | Possibly, if the operator types names                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `plate_recognizer`                 | Plate reads from the [Plate Recognizer](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/add-ons/plate-recognizer/index.md) add-on                                          | Yes                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

The [radar](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/data-and-payloads/radar-payload/index.md) tables are described on their own page. The two tables below have no other page.

### deployment

A row for each combination of sensor, survey, and bearing the device has had, taken from the `deployment` settings in [config.yml](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/configuration/node-red-config/#deployment). A new row starts when the survey id or the sensor's bearing changes; moving the coordinates alone does not start one. Every other table's `deployment_id` column holds the `id` of one of these rows, so you can tell where a reading was taken after the device has moved. The database declares no foreign key; it's a plain text column.

| Column               | Type              | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------------- | ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                 | TEXT, primary key | The deployment id                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `entryStartDateTime` | REAL              | Unix time, in milliseconds, when this deployment began                                                                                                                                                     |
| `entryEndDateTime`   | REAL              | Unix time, in milliseconds, when it ended; empty for the current one                                                                                                                                       |
| `survey_id`          | TEXT              | The place: one id for each place the device has been used at, such as `3f9a1c2e-si`. It has no coordinates in it, so rows at the same place share it. Empty when no survey id was set.                     |
| `location_precision` | INTEGER           | The number of decimal places kept in `lat` and `lon`: `1` (about 10 km) or `2` (about 1 km). Empty when the row has no coordinates.                                                                        |
| `lat`                | REAL              | Latitude in decimal degrees, rounded to `location_precision` decimal places; empty when no location was given or the precision is `none`                                                                   |
| `lon`                | REAL              | Longitude in decimal degrees, rounded the same way                                                                                                                                                         |
| `bearing`            | TEXT              | Compass direction the sensor faces: `n`, `s`, `e`, `w`, `ne`, `nw`, `se`, or `sw`. Empty when no bearing was set; closed rows written by earlier releases can hold `null` or `undefined` instead.          |
| `sensorType`         | TEXT              | `cameras`, `radars`, or `airquality_monitors`                                                                                                                                                              |
| `sensorName`         | TEXT              | The sensor's name in `config.yml`                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `deviceName`         | TEXT              | The Raspberry Pi's serial number (`TM_RPI_SN` in [node-red-tm.env](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/configuration/environment/index.md)). Rows written by earlier releases can hold `undefined` instead. |

The database holds shareable data only, so the exact location is never written to it. A database upgraded from a release that stored exact coordinates holds rounded ones. When Node-RED first starts after the upgrade, the database migration copies the database to `db/backup/tmdb-v<N>-<time>.sqlite` in the `node-red-tm` directory, where N is the schema version the device was on before, and that copy holds the exact rows. A device upgrading from a release (0.7.1 or earlier) has `tmdb-v0-…`, and a device that already ran a development build with the first schema version has `tmdb-v1-…`. The copy is kept until the next schema change succeeds. You can delete it sooner, once the control app has read the past places from it; see [Places after an update](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/build-your-own-device-diy/update/#places-after-an-update). The first upgrade from a release copies the whole database, so it needs free space of about 1.2 times the database's size. If the disk was too full for the copy, it was skipped and the exact coordinates are gone.

### comments

Free-text notes an operator adds on the [Data export](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/ui/database/index.md) page, for example "threshold lowered to 0.4" or "road work on the north side", so that whoever analyzes the data later knows what changed and when.

| Column               | Type              | Meaning                                     |
| -------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                 | TEXT, primary key |                                             |
| `effectiveDateTime`  | TIMESTAMP         | When the note starts to apply               |
| `expirationDateTime` | TIMESTAMP         | When it stops applying; empty if open-ended |
| `entryDateTime`      | TIMESTAMP         | When it was written                         |
| `comment`            | TEXT              | The note                                    |
| `commenter_name`     | TEXT              | Who wrote it                                |

### Schema versions

The tables are defined by numbered migrations in the repository's [`container/node-red-tm/schema/`](https://github.com/glossyio/traffic-monitor/tree/main/container/node-red-tm/schema) folder, and `schema.sql` there shows the whole current schema. Each time the Node-RED service starts, it applies any migrations the database doesn't have yet and records the schema version in the database. Before it does, it saves a copy of the database in `/opt/traffic-monitor/node-red-tm/db/backup/` and keeps only the most recent copy. It makes no copy of a new database, or when the disk has less free space than about 1.2 times the database's size. It also makes none when the only migration to apply is the first, which only adds missing tables. You can read the version with `PRAGMA user_version;`.

If a migration fails, it's rolled back, and Node-RED starts on the previous version, which may not be able to save new data. The control app's [Status page](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/device-health/#the-status-page) then shows **Database schema** as a problem. To see why, run `sudo journalctl -u node-red-tm | grep tmdb-migrate`, or download the diagnostics on the Device page. See [the FAQ entry](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/help-and-faq/frequently-asked-questions/#troubleshooting).

## Getting the data

- **Download** the whole database, or a JSON export of events, radar readings, or air quality readings over a date range, from the [Data export](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/ui/database/index.md) page.
- **Open** the database with [DB Browser for SQLite](https://sqlitebrowser.org/), or from code with any SQLite library, such as Python's built-in `sqlite3`.
- **Subscribe** to today's counts over MQTT, or **upload** everything to ThingsBoard. See [MQTT and ThingsBoard](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/data-and-payloads/integrations/index.md).
- **Review** snapshots and clips in Frigate's **Explore** view at `http://<device>/frigate/`.

______________________________________________________________________

## description: The events table: one row per object the camera detected, with its label, times, zones, direction, and radar speed.

# Events

An event is one object that Frigate detected and tracked until it left the frame: a car, a person, a bicycle, and so on. When the camera has a radar, the Traffic Monitor adds the direction of travel and the speed, and it stores the result in the `events` table of the database.

## How an event is made

1. Frigate publishes a message on the device's MQTT topic `frigate/events` for each tracked object. When the object leaves the frame, the message has `type: "end"` and holds everything Frigate knows about it.
1. The Traffic Monitor keeps the `end` message if the camera is enabled in [config.yml](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/configuration/node-red-config/#sensorscameras) and the object moved.
1. If the object entered any zone and the camera has an enabled radar, it works out the direction and the speed, as described below, and adds `radar` to `provenance` when a speed was found.
1. It writes the row, publishes today's counts on `tm/events`, and uploads the event to ThingsBoard if that is on. See [MQTT and ThingsBoard](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/data-and-payloads/integrations/index.md).

[First-time setup](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/setup-guide/#3-adjust-the-zones) describes the four zones.

## Direction and speed

The zones give a direction when the object entered both `zone_near` and `zone_far`: `zone_near` then `zone_far` is outbound, and the reverse is inbound. The radar's readings come from the time the object was in view, with a two-second margin on each side. The radar reports a direction with each reading, and the speed is the median of the readings in the chosen direction.

| Zones        | Radar readings                           | `direction_calc`      | `speed_calc`                 |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------- | --------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| A direction  | In that direction, or in both directions | The zones' direction  | The median in that direction |
| A direction  | Only in the other direction              | Empty                 | Empty                        |
| No direction | In one direction only                    | The radar's direction | The median in that direction |
| No direction | In both directions                       | Empty                 | Empty                        |
| A direction  | None                                     | The zones' direction  | Empty                        |
| No direction | None                                     | Empty                 | Empty                        |

An object that entered no zone, and every object on a camera without an enabled radar, has no direction and no speed.

## Columns

Values that come straight from Frigate's message are marked *Frigate*. Frigate's [MQTT](https://docs.frigate.video/integrations/mqtt) page documents them in full.

| Column             | Type              | Meaning                                                                                                                           | Values                                                                                                               |
| ------------------ | ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`               | TEXT, primary key | Frigate's event id                                                                                                                | Unix time in seconds, a hyphen, and six random characters, such as `1721144705.617111-fg3luy`                        |
| `camera`           | TEXT              | *Frigate.* The camera's name                                                                                                      | As named in Frigate, `picam_h265` by default                                                                         |
| `label`            | TEXT              | *Frigate.* The object type                                                                                                        | One of Frigate's [object labels](https://docs.frigate.video/configuration/objects)                                   |
| `sub_label`        | TEXT              | *Frigate.* A label added by another process, such as a recognized face                                                            | Usually empty                                                                                                        |
| `top_score`        | REAL              | *Frigate.* The highest detection score while the object was tracked                                                               | 0 to 1                                                                                                               |
| `frame_time`       | REAL              | *Frigate.* When the best frame of the object was taken                                                                            | Unix time in seconds                                                                                                 |
| `start_time`       | REAL              | *Frigate.* When the object was first seen                                                                                         | Unix time in seconds                                                                                                 |
| `end_time`         | REAL              | *Frigate.* When the object was last seen                                                                                          | Unix time in seconds                                                                                                 |
| `entered_zones`    | TEXT              | *Frigate.* The zones the object entered, in order                                                                                 | A JSON array of zone names, such as `["zone_capture", "zone_near", "zone_radar", "zone_far"]`                        |
| `score`            | REAL              | *Frigate.* The object's current score when the event ended                                                                        | 0 to 1                                                                                                               |
| `area`             | REAL              | *Frigate.* Width × height of the object's box, in pixels                                                                          |                                                                                                                      |
| `ratio`            | REAL              | *Frigate.* Width ÷ height of the object's box                                                                                     | Less than 1 is taller than wide                                                                                      |
| `motionless_count` | REAL              | *Frigate.* Frames in which the object didn't move                                                                                 | A count                                                                                                              |
| `position_changes` | REAL              | *Frigate.* How many times the object changed position                                                                             | A count                                                                                                              |
| `attributes`       | TEXT              | *Frigate.* Attributes detected on the object, with their best scores                                                              | A JSON object, such as `{"face": 0.86}`; usually empty                                                               |
| `direction_calc`   | TEXT              | Direction of travel relative to the device                                                                                        | `outbound` (away from the device), `inbound` (toward it), or empty. See [Direction and speed](#direction-and-speed). |
| `speed_calc`       | REAL              | Speed from the radar, in the radar's units (mph by default)                                                                       | Positive for inbound and negative for outbound; empty if no speed was matched                                        |
| `provenance`       | TEXT              | Which sensors contributed, primary first                                                                                          | A JSON array: `["frigate"]`, or `["frigate", "radar"]` when a speed was matched                                      |
| `radarName`        | TEXT              | The radar paired with the camera, if that radar is enabled, whether or not it supplied a speed                                    | A radar name such as `TM_RADAR_SERIAL_PORT_00`, or empty                                                             |
| `deployment_id`    | TEXT              | Where the device was. See the [deployment](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/data-and-payloads/data-overview/#deployment) table. | A `deployment.id`, or empty                                                                                          |

# MQTT and ThingsBoard

The MQTT broker is on by default and accepts connections only from the device itself. The ThingsBoard upload is off until you turn it on.

## MQTT

Node-RED hosts an MQTT broker on the device at port `1883`. Frigate, the air quality sensor, and Node-RED connect to it on the device. Other devices on your network, such as Home Assistant or a display board that shows the day's counts, can connect once you give the broker a login; see [Connect from other devices](#connect-from-other-devices). Settings are in [node-red-tm.env](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/configuration/environment/index.md).

| Topic                                | Direction                                                                                                    | Contents                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `frigate/events`                     | Frigate to the Traffic Monitor                                                                               | Frigate's [event messages](https://docs.frigate.video/integrations/mqtt). The Traffic Monitor records the ones with `type: "end"` as [events](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/data-and-payloads/events-payload/index.md).                                                                                                 |
| `frigate/<camera>/<object>/snapshot` | Frigate to subscribers                                                                                       | A cropped JPEG of each detected object, which can show a person. Frigate publishes it only when the camera's `mqtt` setting is on, and new installs turn it off. The Traffic Monitor doesn't use it. See [Tune object detection](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/configuration/frigate-config/#recordings-and-snapshots). |
| `aq/<sensor>/readings`               | [Air quality sensor](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/add-ons/air-quality/index.md) to the Traffic Monitor | One JSON reading. See [Air quality](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/data-and-payloads/air-quality-aq-payload/index.md).                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `tm/events`                          | The Traffic Monitor to subscribers                                                                           | Today's cumulative counts, mainly for a display board. Published with QoS 1 and retained, so a new subscriber gets the latest counts at once. See below.                                                                                                                                                                     |

`tm/event`, without the `s`, is the per-event message inside Node-RED. Each recorded event carries it to the dashboards and to the ThingsBoard upload. It isn't published on the broker, so MQTT clients such as Home Assistant can't subscribe to it.

### tm/events

A JSON object with the same counts as **Today's counts** on the [Monitoring](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/ui/monitoring/index.md) dashboard: events that passed through `zone_capture`, for the camera selected on the legacy dashboard at `http://<device>/ui/`, in a day that starts at 04:00 local time.

| Key                                                         | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `car`, `person`, `bicycle`, `motorcycle`, `bus`, `dog`, ... | One key per object type that has been counted today, named as Frigate labels it                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `bicycle_adj`                                               | `bicycle` plus `motorcycle`. Present once a bicycle has been counted.                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `person_adj`                                                | `person` minus `bicycle` minus `motorcycle`: a pedestrian count, because every cyclist is also detected as a person. Scooter riders count as people. It can be negative, when more bicycles and motorcycles than people have been counted. Present once a person has been counted. |
| `event_latest`                                              | The object type of the most recent counted event, such as `car`                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

To watch it from another computer:

```
mosquitto_sub -h <device> -u <username> -P <password> -t tm/events
```

### Connect from other devices

1. Give the broker a login:

   ```
   bash traffic-monitor/script/tmsetup.sh -t node-red-tm -C mqtt_lan
   ```

   This creates the username `tm` and a random password. To choose your own instead, set `TM_MQTT_BROKER_USERNAME` and `TM_MQTT_BROKER_PASSWORD` in `/opt/traffic-monitor/node-red-tm/node-red-tm.env` and run the command without `-C mqtt_lan`. Use only letters, digits, `.`, `_`, and `-`, with no quotes and no comment after the value on the same line; otherwise the installer stops with a message.

   The broker then requires the login from every client, the installer gives it to Frigate, and port 1883 opens to your network.

1. Read the login:

   ```
   sudo grep ^TM_MQTT_BROKER_ /opt/traffic-monitor/node-red-tm/node-red-tm.env
   ```

1. Give it to the [air quality sensor](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/add-ons/air-quality/index.md) and to each MQTT client.

1. Check from another computer:

   ```
   mosquitto_sub -h <device> -u <username> -P <password> -t tm/events
   ```

1. To change the login, edit the two values and run `bash traffic-monitor/script/tmsetup.sh -t node-red-tm` again. To remove it, leave both values blank and run the same command: the broker stops checking logins and port 1883 closes to the network.

Warning

The login crosses the network unencrypted, and anyone who has it can read every topic and publish false data. Open MQTT only on a network you trust.

## ThingsBoard

The device can upload its data to a [ThingsBoard](https://thingsboard.io/) server, which gives you dashboards and storage for a fleet of devices. Turn it on in the `thingsboard` section of [config.yml](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/configuration/node-red-config/#thingsboard) with the server's hostname, and enter the device's access token on the control app's [Device page](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/use/device-health/#tokens-and-keys). Saving the token restarts Node-RED, which takes about thirty seconds. The device picks up a change to the file when you save it.

Once connected, the device sends over ThingsBoard's HTTP API:

- Each [event](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/data-and-payloads/events-payload/index.md) as telemetry, with `ts` set to the event's `frame_time` in milliseconds and `values` holding every column of the event.
- Each [radar](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/data-and-payloads/radar-payload/index.md) and [air quality](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/data-and-payloads/air-quality-aq-payload/index.md) reading as telemetry. Readings from the high-rate radar tables are batched to avoid hundreds of messages per vehicle.
- The device's system metrics as telemetry, every five minutes.
- The deployment location, radar information, and the Traffic Monitor settings as device attributes.

### Config backup

With ThingsBoard connected, the **Backup & Restore** section of the legacy dashboard at `http://<device>/ui/` saves Frigate's config as an attribute of the device in ThingsBoard.

______________________________________________________________________

## description: The five radar tables: detected object velocities, timed counts, raw speed and magnitude readings, and per-object summaries.

# Radar

The [OmniPreSense OPS243-A](https://omnipresense.com/product/ops243-doppler-radar-sensor/) Doppler radar measures the speed and direction of whatever moves in front of it, does its own signal processing, and reports readings over USB as JSON. The Traffic Monitor turns on several of the radar's reporting modes when the service starts and whenever config.yml is saved, and stores each kind of reading in its own table. The radar's [API guide](https://omnipresense.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/AN-010-Y_API_Interface.pdf) describes the modes and the commands.

| Reading                  | Radar command                | Table                              | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Detected object velocity | `ON`                         | `radar_dov`                        | The radar decides an object is present when it sees two consecutive speed reports, then reports the highest speed, and again if a higher one follows. One or a few readings per object. These readings supply the speeds for [events](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/data-and-payloads/events-payload/index.md). |
| Timed speed counts       | `@O`, every 300 seconds      | `radar_timed_speed_counts`         | How many objects passed in each direction during the interval, and their average speed                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Raw speed and magnitude  | `OS` and `OM` with `O3`      | `radar_raw_speed_magnitude`        | The three strongest speed and magnitude pairs from each sample. Magnitude reflects the object's size, distance, and reflectivity.                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Strongest reading        | the first of the three above | `radar_raw_speed_magnitude_single` | The single strongest pair from each sample, for easier analysis                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Object summary           | `OC`                         | `radar_oc_payload`                 | One row per object, with its time in view, speed range, magnitude, and estimated length. Needs OPS9243 firmware.                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

Across the tables, `direction` is `inbound` (toward the radar) or `outbound` (away from it), speeds are positive for inbound and negative for outbound, and the unit is the radar's speed unit, mph by default. `radarName` is the radar's name from [config.yml](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/configuration/node-red-config/#sensorsradars), and `deployment_id` points at the [deployment](https://docs.trafficmonitor.ai/dev/data-and-payloads/data-overview/#deployment) the reading was taken in.

The times come from the radar's own clock, which starts again from zero whenever the radar loses power. The Traffic Monitor sets that clock from the device's clock when the service starts, whenever config.yml is saved, every hour, and within about half a minute of a radar being plugged back in.

## radar_dov

| Column          | Type | Meaning                           | Values                              |
| --------------- | ---- | --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `time`          | REAL | When the radar took the reading   | Unix time in seconds                |
| `unit`          | TEXT | Speed unit                        | `mph`                               |
| `direction`     | TEXT | Direction of travel               | `inbound` or `outbound`             |
| `velocity`      | REAL | The object's highest speed so far | Positive inbound, negative outbound |
| `radarName`     | TEXT | The radar                         |                                     |
| `deployment_id` | TEXT | The deployment                    |                                     |

## radar_timed_speed_counts

| Column          | Type    | Meaning                                                | Values                              |
| --------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------- |
| `time`          | REAL    | End of the interval                                    | Unix time in seconds                |
| `direction`     | TEXT    | Direction of travel                                    | `inbound` or `outbound`             |
| `units`         | TEXT    | Speed unit                                             | `mph`                               |
| `count`         | INTEGER | Objects detected in this direction during the interval | 0 or more                           |
| `average`       | REAL    | Their average speed                                    | Positive inbound, negative outbound |
| `radarName`     | TEXT    | The radar                                              |                                     |
| `deployment_id` | TEXT    | The deployment                                         |                                     |

## radar_raw_speed_magnitude

| Column          | Type | Meaning                                                       | Values                                            |
| --------------- | ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `time`          | REAL | When the sample was taken                                     | Unix time in seconds                              |
| `unit`          | TEXT | Speed unit                                                    | `mph`                                             |
| `magnitude`     | TEXT | The three strongest magnitudes in the sample, strongest first | A JSON array of positive numbers                  |
| `speed`         | TEXT | The speeds that go with each magnitude                        | A JSON array; positive inbound, negative outbound |
| `radarName`     | TEXT | The radar                                                     |                                                   |
| `deployment_id` | TEXT | The deployment                                                |                                                   |

## radar_raw_speed_magnitude_single

| Column          | Type | Meaning                               | Values                              |
| --------------- | ---- | ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `time`          | REAL | When the sample was taken             | Unix time in seconds                |
| `unit`          | TEXT | Speed unit                            | `mph`                               |
| `magnitude`     | REAL | The strongest magnitude in the sample | Positive                            |
| `speed`         | REAL | The speed that goes with it           | Positive inbound, negative outbound |
| `radarName`     | TEXT | The radar                             |                                     |
| `deployment_id` | TEXT | The deployment                        |                                     |

## radar_oc_payload

| Column                | Type | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Values                                                  |
| --------------------- | ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `start_time`          | REAL | When the object entered the radar's view                                                                                                                                                                                              | Unix time in seconds                                    |
| `end_time`            | REAL | When it left                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Unix time in seconds                                    |
| `delta_time_msec`     | REAL | Time in view                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Milliseconds                                            |
| `direction`           | TEXT | Direction of travel                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | `inbound` or `outbound`                                 |
| `frames_count`        | REAL | Radar frames in which the object was seen                                                                                                                                                                                             | A count                                                 |
| `velocity_max`        | REAL | Highest speed while in view                                                                                                                                                                                                           |                                                         |
| `velocity_min`        | REAL | Lowest speed while in view                                                                                                                                                                                                            |                                                         |
| `magnitude_max`       | REAL | Highest magnitude while in view                                                                                                                                                                                                       |                                                         |
| `magnitude_mean`      | REAL | Average magnitude while in view                                                                                                                                                                                                       |                                                         |
| `velocity_change`     | REAL | The change in speed while in view, as the radar reports it. A vehicle at the edge of the radar's view shows a larger change, from the cosine effect, so this hints at which lane it was in. Dividing by `velocity_max` normalizes it. | Empty for radars whose report format doesn't include it |
| `frames_per_velocity` | REAL | `frames_count` ÷ `velocity_max`, the inverse of speed used to estimate length                                                                                                                                                         |                                                         |
| `object_length`       | REAL | Estimated length, from speed and time in view                                                                                                                                                                                         | Feet for `imperial`, metres for `metric`                |
| `units`               | TEXT | Unit system                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | `imperial` or `metric`                                  |
| `object_label`        | TEXT | Reserved for a radar-based object classification                                                                                                                                                                                      | Always empty                                            |
| `radarName`           | TEXT | The radar                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |                                                         |
| `deployment_id`       | TEXT | The deployment                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |                                                         |
# Add-ons
